aspect: The share of the world's maternal deaths
description: Estimates vary by source and year: roughly 40,000 pregnancy-related deaths annually, about 14% of the global total; a WHO-based figure puts it at 58,000, 19.1% of 303,000. Nigeria is among the top six countries contributing more than half of all global maternal deaths.
energy_note: One country, a seventh to a fifth of all maternal deaths on earth.

description: A maternal mortality ratio of 512 per 100,000 live births nationally, and over 1,000 per 100,000 in northern Nigeria. Maternal deaths account for roughly a third of all deaths among women of reproductive age.
energy_note: A third of all deaths of women of childbearing age.

description: Nigeria's own national framework put it at 4 maternal deaths per hour, 90 per day, 2,800 per month - about 34,000 annually - with at least 30 women suffering short- or long-term morbidity for every death.
energy_note: Four an hour, ninety a day, every day.

aspect: Only 43% of births have a skilled attendant
description: Which is the single most modifiable number in this entire category, and the one that determines whether an obstructed labour becomes a caesarean or becomes MAT-002.
energy_note: More than half of births, with nobody trained present.

aspect: The delays are geographic and financial before they are clinical
description: Deciding to seek care, reaching a facility, and receiving care on arrival. The first is about money and permission, the second about roads and transport, the third about staffing and the deposit in HLT-001.
energy_note: Three delays, and the clinical one is last.

aspect: SCENARIO - the night before the market day
description: Labour starts at 23:00. The nearest facility with a theatre is 40km on a road nobody drives after dark. The traditional birth attendant is eleven minutes away. They wait for morning. It is the decision that most families in that village make, and it is usually right.
energy_note: Waiting for daylight, and usually being correct.
